correctness.rationale: For d>=2,m>=3 the symmetric polarization of F=x0^(m-1)*x_(d-1)+x0^(m-2)*sum_(1<=i<=d-2) xi^2 has all d partial derivatives linearly independent: the first partial separates x_(d-1), the remaining monomial derivatives are independent, and the last coordinate derivative is x0^(m-1). Each mode flattening has rank d. Simultaneous determinant-one weights (d-1,-1,...,-1) give strictly positive weights (m-1)(d-1)-1 and (m-2)(d-1)-2 except d=m=3; at (3,3), (2,0,-2) gives weight 2 for both monomials. Thus T tends to zero under an SL_d^m one-parameter subgroup, forcing every positive-character semi-invariant to vanish: it is not central semistable. For m=2, invertible matrices lie in the GL_d x GL_d orbit of I_d, a balanced polystable representative. I independently recomputed flattening ranks and occupied-term 1PS weights for 42 finite formats; these checks corroborate and do not establish the universal quantifiers.
residual_risks: Finite independent tests corroborate only tested parameters; universal argument is from source proof and standard theorem applications.
